result.topic: PAN-OS REST API v11.0 field/tag confirmation for Objects/URLFilteringSecurityProfiles and Objects/AntiSpywareSecurityProfiles, including DNS Security sub-fields inside the Anti-Spyware profile

confirmedFacts.claim: REST resource paths are /restapi/v11.0/Objects/AntiSpywareSecurityProfiles and /restapi/v11.0/Objects/URLFilteringSecurityProfiles (v11.0 version segment used even on PAN-OS 11.1 doc pages).
confirmedFacts.evidence: "/restapi/v11.0/Objects/AntiSpywareSecurityProfiles" and "/restapi/v11.0/Objects/URLFilteringSecurityProfiles" listed in the Objects resource table

confirmedFacts.claim: PAN-OS REST API JSON mirrors XML tag names verbatim, including hyphens (kebab-case), not camelCase or snake_case. XML attributes (e.g. entry name, location, vsys) become JSON keys prefixed with '@'. XML <member> lists become a JSON array nested under a "member" key, not a bare array replacing the field.

REST GET response envelope is {"result": {"@count":..., "@total-count":..., "entry": [ {...}, {...} ]}} — entries appear directly under result.entry, with no extra object-type wrapper key. This confirms the existing prototype code's `data.get('result', {}).get('entry', [])` access pattern is structurally correct.

github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/pan-os-python does NOT contain any AntiSpywareProfile, URLFilteringProfile, VulnerabilityProfile, or DNS-security/botnet-domain class anywhere in panos/objects.py (or any other module). This SDK does not model security profile *content* at all — SecurityProfileGroup only references profile names as plain strings (vartype=member), it does not build/parse profile bodies. Verified directly against both the 'develop' branch HEAD and the latest stable tag v1.13.1 by fetching and grepping the raw file.
confirmedFacts.evidence: grep of class definitions in objects.py yields only: AddressObject, AddressGroup, Tag, ServiceObject, ServiceGroup, ApplicationObject, ApplicationGroup, ApplicationTag, ApplicationFilter, ApplicationContainer, SecurityProfileGroup, CustomUrlCategory, LogForwardingProfile(+MatchList/+Action), DynamicUserGroup, ScheduleObject, Region, Edl — no Spyware/URLFiltering/DNS classes exist

confirmedFacts.claim: The task's premise that pan-os-python's panos/objects.py has an AntiSpywareProfile class encoding real field names is WRONG — that class does not exist in this SDK at any checked revision. It cannot be used as a source for these field names.
confirmedFacts.evidence: readthedocs module-objects page class list has no AntiSpywareProfile/URLFilteringProfile entries; matches direct source grep

confirmedFacts.claim: Confirmed exact XML/config-tree shape of the Anti-Spyware ('spyware') profile for PAN-OS 11.0 (same generation as Suncoast's 11.1.13/11.2.10 targets), from Palo Alto Networks' own official best-practice config template repo (Iron Skillet), version-pinned file panos_v11.0/panorama/panorama_profiles_spyware_11_0.skillet.yaml, xpath /config/shared/profiles/spyware: top-level <entry name="..."> containing <botnet-domains> (wrapping <lists><entry name="default-paloalto-dns"><action><sinkhole/></action><packet-capture>...</packet-capture></entry></lists>, <dns-security-categories><entry name="pan-dns-sec-<cat>"><log-level>default</log-level><action>default|sinkhole</action><packet-capture>disable|single-packet</packet-capture></entry>...</dns-security-categories>, <sinkhole><ipv4-address>...</ipv4-address><ipv6-address>...</ipv6-address></sinkhole>), plus sibling <rules>, <mica-engine-spyware-enabled>, <cloud-inline-analysis>. The 9 DNS category entry names are: pan-dns-sec-benign, pan-dns-sec-cc, pan-dns-sec-ddns, pan-dns-sec-grayware, pan-dns-sec-malware, pan-dns-sec-parked, pan-dns-sec-phishing, pan-dns-sec-proxy, pan-dns-sec-recent. Identical structure confirmed also in the 10.1 version of the same file, i.e. this shape is stable across the 10.1-11.0 line.

IMPORTANT NAMING TRAP: the WebUI-documented label for the DNS category logging control is "Log Severity", but the actual underlying tag confirmed in the Iron Skillet XML for dns-security-categories entries is <log-level>, NOT <log-severity>. Do not assume the JSON/XML key is 'log-severity' for this sub-field just because that's the UI label and because 'log-severity' does exist elsewhere in the schema (URL Filtering profile's credential-enforcement block genuinely uses <log-severity>). The two profile types use different tag names for logically similar settings.
confirmedFacts.evidence: dns-security-categories entries use <log-level>default</log-level>; url-filtering profile's credential-enforcement block uses <log-severity>high</log-severity> (from panorama_profiles_url_filtering_11_0.skillet.yaml)

confirmedFacts.claim: Confirmed action-value vocabulary for DNS security category action tag includes literal strings 'default' and 'sinkhole' (from real Iron Skillet config); official WebUI prose additionally documents 'alert', 'allow', 'block' as selectable Policy Action choices for DNS Signature Policies, with sinkhole as PAN-OS's default action for Palo Alto Networks DNS signatures.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "Policy Action... alert, allow, block, or sinkhole"; "The default action for Palo Alto Networks DNS signatures is sinkhole."

confirmedFacts.claim: Confirmed exact XML/config-tree shape of the URL Filtering ('url-filtering') security profile for PAN-OS 11.0, same official Iron Skillet repo, xpath /config/shared/profiles/url-filtering: top-level <entry> with per-action category-membership lists — <alert><member>category-name</member>...</alert> and <block><member>...</member></block> — plus <credential-enforcement><mode><ip-user/></mode><log-severity>high</log-severity><block>|<alert>...</credential-enforcement>, and simple booleans <log-http-hdr-user-agent>yes</log-http-hdr-user-agent>, <log-http-hdr-referer>, <log-http-hdr-xff>, <local-inline-cat>, <cloud-inline-cat>. Category name strings themselves (e.g. malware, phishing, command-and-control, dynamic-dns, encrypted-dns, newly-registered-domain) are also confirmed verbatim from this source.

No official REST-JSON worked example exists anywhere for AntiSpywareSecurityProfiles or URLFilteringSecurityProfiles specifically (confirmed by exhaustive search of docs.paloaltonetworks.com and pan.dev). The exact JSON encoding of self-closing XML 'choice' elements (e.g. <action><sinkhole/></action>, <action><reset-both/></action>) — i.e. whether this becomes {"action":{"sinkhole":{}}}, {"action":{"sinkhole":null}}, or {"action":"sinkhole"} in REST JSON for the botnet-domains 'lists' sub-object specifically — is NOT directly confirmed by any official example for this object. This is inferred, not confirmed, by analogy to the general convention.
confirmedFacts.evidence: page explicitly defers all object/field schema to on-device /restapi-doc and confirms no Swagger/OpenAPI browser exists publicly for these objects

confirmedFacts.claim: No public Swagger/OpenAPI browser for PAN-OS REST API objects exists on pan.dev or docs.paloaltonetworks.com. The only authoritative, complete, field-level schema reference is the on-device https://<device>/restapi-doc, which requires live device access — confirming this cannot be closed from public sources alone.
confirmedFacts.evidence: page links only to prose docs and to on-device documentation at https://HOSTNAME/restapi; no embedded schema browser present

remainingGaps: Exact JSON encoding of self-closing XML 'choice' sub-elements (e.g. <action><sinkhole/></action> under botnet-domains/lists, <action><reset-both/></action> under rules) is not confirmed for AntiSpywareSecurityProfiles specifically by any official worked JSON example — only inferred from the general REST convention shown for unrelated objects (address/security-rule). Needs a live GET against a real profile to see whether it renders as {"sinkhole":{}}, {"sinkhole":null}, or something else.

Whether the top-level REST GET response for AntiSpywareSecurityProfiles nests fields directly under each result.entry item (as this research assumes, matching every other confirmed object type) or introduces some additional wrapper specific to security profiles is not verified with a literal official JSON example of THIS object — inferred from the general, confirmed result/entry pattern, not object-specific.

The full enumerated action tag set for URLFilteringSecurityProfiles beyond <alert>/<block> (i.e. whether <allow>, <continue>, <override> exist as sibling tags in the current 11.x schema, and whether 'override' still exists at all in 11.x given it was product-deprecated in some PAN-OS versions) was not directly observed in the two Iron Skillet 11.0 examples fetched (they only used alert/block) — this is a real open gap, not just an inference gap.

Threat Exception tab fields for the Anti-Spyware profile (<threat-exception>, per-signature override structure) were not present in any Iron Skillet example examined and remain completely unconfirmed by any source in this research pass.

Whether PAN-OS 11.1.13 / 11.2.10-H3 (Suncoast's actual fleet versions, one minor rev above the 11.0 Iron Skillet source used here) preserves this exact tag set unchanged, versus adding/renaming any field, cannot be confirmed from public sources — Iron Skillet has no 11.1 or 11.2 branch published, only 10.0/10.1/10.2/11.0. The 10.1->11.0 stability observed (identical dns-security-categories shape across those versions) supports low risk of drift, but is not proof for 11.1/11.2.

No live device / Palo Alto support access means none of this can be cross-checked against the device's own authoritative /restapi-doc, which Palo Alto explicitly states is the only complete, version-pinned schema reference.

recommendedCodeChanges.change: In get_dns_security_profiles()'s docstring, replace the blanket 'DNS-Security-specific sub-fields... NOT confirmed' statement with the now-confirmed shape: each entry's DNS Security settings live under entry['botnet-domains'], which itself contains 'lists' (EDL/botnet-list-based entries with 'action' + 'packet-capture'), 'dns-security-categories' (an entry-array of the 9 pan-dns-sec-* categories, each with 'log-level' [not 'log-severity'], 'action', 'packet-capture'), and 'sinkhole' ({'ipv4-address':..., 'ipv6-address':...}). Cite the Iron Skillet source. Keep flagged as unconfirmed only the exact JSON encoding of the self-closing <action><sinkhole/></action> choice element for list-based entries specifically, and add a note to log/inspect the raw response the first time this runs against a real Suncoast device to verify that one remaining detail before parsing it structurally.

Add a helper (e.g. get_dns_security_categories(entry) -> list) that reads entry.get('botnet-domains', {}).get('dns-security-categories', {}).get('entry', []) and normalizes each item's '@name', 'log-level', 'action', 'packet-capture' into a flat dict — this is now safe to implement given the confirmed shape, rather than leaving all DNS-specific parsing unimplemented pending live verification.

Update section 3 ('Security Profiles') to record the now-confirmed field/tag names for AntiSpywareSecurityProfiles' DNS Security sub-structure (botnet-domains > lists / dns-security-categories / sinkhole) and for URLFilteringSecurityProfiles (per-action category-membership lists: alert, block, plus credential-enforcement/log-severity/log-http-hdr-*), citing github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/ironskillet-components (panos_v11.0 skillet YAMLs) as the source, and explicitly correct the assumption that github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/pan-os-python's objects.py models these profiles — confirmed it does not, at any version checked.

Add a callout under 'Items That Must Be Confirmed Against a Live Suncoast Firewall': the exact JSON encoding of choice-type XML sub-elements (self-closing tags like <sinkhole/> or <reset-both/> nested inside <action>) is still unconfirmed for these two specific objects, and the schema was only confirmed at the PAN-OS 11.0 config-template level (Iron Skillet has no 11.1/11.2 branch) — one minor-version extrapolation gap remains even after this research pass.
